stem: What does the 'acyclic' in DAG guarantee for an Airflow workflow?

options.text: Tasks can run in any order
options.why: Order is defined by the edges, not arbitrary.

options.text: A deterministic, finite run order exists
options.why: No cycles means dependencies resolve to a clear order.
Acyclicity is about ordering, not failure.
Dependencies still serialize connected tasks.

explanation: Without cycles, dependencies resolve into a finite, well-defined execution order — the basis for scheduling.

stem: A daily Airflow DAG has logical date 2026-09-10. When does that run actually start?

options.why: The interval must complete before the run fires.
Runs fire at the end of the data interval they cover.
Firing is tied to interval end, not a fixed clock time.
Only one interval's length passes, not a week.

explanation: Airflow fires a run at the END of its data interval, since the interval's data only exists once it is over.

stem: Which executor gives per-task isolation by running each task in its own pod?

options.why: Local runs tasks as subprocesses on one host.
Celery uses a shared pool of warm workers.
It launches one pod per task instance.
Sequential runs one task at a time locally.

explanation: KubernetesExecutor spins up a pod per task for isolation and elasticity, at the cost of pod startup latency.

stem: Why can many poke-mode sensors stall an Airflow cluster?

options.why: The issue is slot occupancy, not corruption.

options.text: Each holds a worker slot while waiting
options.why: Poke mode occupies a slot for the whole wait.
The scheduler keeps running; workers are exhausted.
Logs are unaffected.

explanation: Poke-mode sensors hold a worker slot the entire time they wait; enough of them starve the cluster. Use reschedule/deferrable.

stem: What kind of data is XCom designed to pass between tasks?

options.why: Big payloads bloat the metadata DB.

options.text: Small values like ids or paths
options.why: XCom travels through the metadata DB; keep it small.
Store files externally and pass a reference.
XCom is not a streaming channel.

explanation: XCom moves small values via the metadata DB; large data should live in storage with only a reference passed.

stem: Why must Airflow tasks be idempotent?

options.why: Idempotency is about correctness, not UI.

options.text: So retries and backfills don't duplicate data
options.why: Re-running an interval must yield the same state.
Parsing is unrelated to idempotency.
Dependencies are unaffected.

explanation: Retries and backfills re-run intervals; only idempotent tasks (overwrite/upsert per interval) avoid duplicating data.

stem: A new daily DAG with a year-old start_date launches 365 runs at once. What caused it?

options.why: Retries re-run a failed task, not whole intervals.
Catchup schedules every interval since start_date.
Workers run tasks; they don't create runs.
Trigger rules gate tasks, not run creation.

explanation: With catchup enabled, enabling a DAG whose start_date is far in the past schedules all missed intervals immediately.

stem: A teardown task must run even when upstream tasks fail. Which trigger rule fits?

options.why: It skips the task if any upstream failed.
It runs once upstreams finish, regardless of outcome.
It needs at least one success, not any completion.
It gates on skips, not on failure.

explanation: all_done runs the task after all upstreams complete whatever their state — the rule for cleanup/teardown tasks.

stem: In Airflow, which component actually runs a task's code?

options.why: It queues ready task instances but doesn't run code.
The UI displays state; it doesn't execute tasks.
The executor runs the queued task instances.
It stores state, not compute.

explanation: The scheduler decides what is ready and queues it; the executor and its workers run the actual task code.

stem: What does the TaskFlow @task decorator handle automatically?

options.why: Scaling is an executor/infra concern.

options.text: Turning functions into tasks and wiring XComs
options.why: Return values become XComs; deps follow calls.
Unrelated to TaskFlow.
Unrelated to TaskFlow.

explanation: TaskFlow makes a decorated function a task and manages XCom from its return value and arguments, cutting boilerplate.

stem: What does expand() enable in modern Airflow?

options.why: It is not about file size.

options.text: Creating one task instance per runtime input
options.why: It fans a task out over a list at run time.
Scheduling still applies.
It maps a task, not DAGs.

explanation: Dynamic task mapping via expand() creates a mapped task instance per element of a runtime list — parallel fan-out without a fixed count.

stem: Where should database credentials for a DAG live?

options.why: That leaks secrets and blocks env promotion.

options.text: In an Airflow Connection / secrets backend
options.why: DAGs reference a conn_id, not raw secrets.
Logs must never hold secrets.
XCom is not a secret store.

explanation: Connections (or a secrets backend) hold credentials so DAG code references a conn_id and can move across environments safely.
